scoring_justification: Recompute average relative temperature and velocity differences from the agent's raw CSV outputs; directly verifies the paper's thermalization claim.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden threshold for relative temperature and velocity differences to determine thermalization regime
hidden_assets.source_provenance: The threshold 0.1 is derived from the paper's qualitative statement that at high density the disparities are largely reduced and the subband curves nearly overlap; it is a reasonable numerical cut-off for 'nearly equal'.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Threshold chosen as a quantitative translation of the paper's observed convergence; a correct reproduction will yield differences well below 0.1 for high-density and well above 0.1 for low-density.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The threshold is not an exact reported paper number but a sensible criterion that a genuine reproduction would meet; it is not an invented random label.

outputs.description: Low-density quasi-2D transport data used to verify that subband temperatures and drift velocities remain disparate (no thermalization).
High-density quasi-2D transport data used to verify that intersubband thermalization occurs (T0e≈T1e, v0≈v1), validating the one-type-of-carriers model.
Low-density quasi-1D transport data used to verify the absence of strong intersubband thermalization.
High-density quasi-1D transport data used to verify that intersubband thermalization occurs in quantum wires, validating the OTCM.

output_contract.notes: Scoring compares average relative subband temperature and velocity differences against publicly undisclosed thresholds to determine whether each system exhibits the expected thermalization (high density) or non-thermalization (low density). The contract does not disclose the threshold values.
